correctness.rationale: For n=2m and nondegenerate alternating polar matrix B, the nontrivial quadratic Gauss sum has magnitude 2^m, and the complete normalized Fourier coefficient at u is ε2^-m(-1)^{Q(B^-1 u)}. Character orthogonality therefore gives K_Q(u,v)=δ_uv/2+ε2^(-m-1)(-1)^{Q^*(u+v)}. Factoring the dual quadratic through its polar form A=B^-1 gives the diagonal congruence K_Q=D[ I/2+ε 2^(-m-1)(J_(n+1)-2 diag(0,A)) ]D, proving the full real spectrum with multiplicity and the stated ambient probability normalization. The inverse of any invertible binary alternating matrix is alternating; its Pfaffian modulo two counts perfect matchings, so precisely the graphs with odd matching count occur and each Gauss sign is realized by a linear refinement. The difference-set identity |X_Q∩(X_Q+h)|=2^(2m-2)+ε2^(m-1) for all h≠0 gives a common pair for each coordinate increment when m≥2, hence all first-band coordinate coefficients vanish if their polynomial vanishes on X_Q; the m=1 signs yield rank 3 or rank 1. Independent exact computations (not the submitted checker) enumerated all 64 labelled simple graphs of order four, verified all 28 invertible adjacency matrices, all 448 linear refinements, the complete signed Gram entries, pair-intersection formula and rank, and found characteristic polynomials with counts 15,12,1 exactly as stated. Independent six-variable examples and symbolic paired-matching spectra m=1..5 corroborate the general proof; the symbolic character-sum, Pfaffian and difference arguments establish unbounded m.
residual_risks: Finite dimension-four enumeration is exhaustive only for the 28 labelled four-vertex graphs; it does not certify the all-dimensional statement without the accompanying algebra.
Restriction singular values use the induced unrenormalized ambient measure, and must be rescaled for conditional measure on the quadratic set.
No higher-Walsh-band, degenerate-quadric or arbitrary-coordinate-change statement is established.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge novelty attaches to the exact inverse-polar-graph spectral transfer for the coordinate first-Walsh restriction, realization of every odd-perfect-matching graph, and the three-class dimension-four compressed-spectrum census. Classical quadratic bent Gauss flatness, translation-design intersection counts and affine/Cayley equivalence cover important premises (including much of sampling injectivity), but the primary statements inspected do not determine this coordinate-compressed operator: a full Cayley graph spectrum and binary-code 2-design parameters are too coarse to determine principal finite-Walsh-band Gram eigenvalues. A published first-band result over odd characteristic handles a fixed split quadratic cone and a larger q-ary frequency set, not all binary alternating polar graphs; the binary symplectic-group Walsh result samples a different object. The exact indexed duplicate of this assigned work was excluded as independent prior art. Legacy Reed–Muller puncturing, Seidel matrix literature and earlier unindexed principal-frame computations remain real historical risks; search nonmatches are not novelty proofs.

Assigned RESULT.md proof and exact four-vertex classification
value.rationale: A natural and mathematically motivated operator is the restriction Gram matrix of constant-plus-coordinate Walsh characters on the zero locus of a nonsingular binary quadratic. Its full spectrum is an exact coordinate-dependent sampling/conditioning invariant, not determined by global Arf or Cayley equivalence class. The transfer to arbitrary invertible binary polar inverse graphs with odd perfect-matching parity is a complete structural parameterization, the rank theorem excludes all sampling degeneracy from dimension four, the sharp matched-pair spectra form an infinite solvable family, and the 28-labelled-graph census is a natural complete first nontrivial case with three distinct spectrum types. Independent reconstruction and coding/graph comparisons indicate this precise combined invariant is not a mere known-table recomputation. Much of its Fourier-flatness and injectivity proof is standard and mathematical depth modest, but the exact graph-realization/census classification has plausible stand-alone use for quadratic sampling frames and coordinate sensitivity.
residual_risks: The graph transfer gives spectra implicitly through eigenvalues of J-2A; it is not a universal closed radical formula for every graph.
The four-vertex table and matched-family condition numbers are exact but by themselves are modest; value attaches to their role in the all-dimensional natural sampling problem.
No claimed extension to higher Walsh degrees, degenerate forms or general affine frequency supports.

limitations: Best-of-knowledge scientific originality does not constitute exhaustive priority certification; classical coding/Seidel-equivalent identity remains possible.
Finite computations do not establish infinite-dimensional conclusions, which are supported by the independent algebraic derivation.
The existing package cannot be safely published with unsanitized operational metadata; publication_plan status not_ready is transport/privacy, not a rejection of the science.
